title: His own instruments: the Martin and the Gretsch
summary: The guitar he bought in St. Louis, the Martin on Jelly Roll Morton sessions, and his Gretsch from 1932.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, in regard to the instrument yourself, you described the one you made and how you bought this one for $25 in St. Louis.
Is that the same one you used in Chicago all those years, the Cook's band and on the Hot Five records?
It's the same one I have right now.
Same instrument you did. And the Jolly Roll Martin records. That's right.
Well, I know I used a guitar on the Jolly Roll Martin records. I have a Martin guitar. Oh, yeah.
And after one you have, what is your guitar now?
Gretsch. How long have you had that?
Is there anything about picking a guitar or even what make you prefer, not to return to make any, commit to commercial, and recommend one over the other? Well, no.

I just wanted a few. There's a good guitar as you can play. I played Martin. Martin is a very good guitar. In fact it was the Tops at one time. Fess had one, he said he liked the tone. They're very good. It's a very thin material. Then Fess got a fancy Gibson with the big sound holes like the violin. Yes. No.
